title: Six-hour sharing recalculation at 3 million Accounts: 4-stage refactor

stages.scenario: A financial services org has 3 million Accounts, an 11-level role hierarchy, and 45 criteria-based sharing rules on Account granting regional branch access. Each quarterly realignment brings UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW errors and a sharing recalculation that runs for six hours. What is the root cause?

options.text: The realignment runs during business hours, so user edits collide with the platform's sharing updates
options.coachingFeedback: Off-hours scheduling reduces collisions with user edits, but the six-hour run comes from the volume of share rows each change recomputes, and that volume is the same at night.

options.text: A handful of integration users own most Accounts, and that ownership skew locks the rows
options.coachingFeedback: Ownership skew causes lock contention on everyday updates. These failures arrive with each realignment, which is when hierarchy and rule changes force share recalculation.

options.text: Each hierarchy or rule change sets off its own share recalculation across millions of Accounts
options.coachingFeedback: Changes to roles, groups, sharing rules, or team membership each start an automatic sharing recalculation. An 11-level hierarchy, past the 10-level guideline, plus 45 criteria-based rules over 3 million Accounts makes a bulk realignment fire many overlapping recalculations that rewrite large numbers of share rows.

stages.scenario: The 11-level hierarchy mirrors the HR org chart, and branch staff get Account access through the 45 criteria-based rules. Each branch works a changing list of specific accounts, and some Accounts are confidential to their branch. Which redesign cuts recalculation cost while keeping that access?

options.text: Set Account to Public Read Only and hide confidential Accounts from other branches with restriction rules
options.coachingFeedback: Restriction rules are available on custom objects, external objects, contracts, events, tasks, and time sheets, not Account, so a Public Read Only default would expose every confidential Account to every branch.

options.text: Reduce roles to data-access levels and give branch staff access through account teams
options.coachingFeedback: Roles should represent levels of data access, not the HR chart, so fewer levels means fewer cascades per change. Account teams grant access account by account, so a team change touches one Account's shares instead of re-evaluating a rule across all 3 million.

options.text: Keep the hierarchy and consolidate the 45 criteria-based rules into a few broader rules
options.coachingFeedback: Fewer rules still grant access by field values, so a realignment that changes those values still recalculates every matching Account, and broader rules overshare confidential Accounts. The 11-level hierarchy stays as well.

stages.scenario: The flatter hierarchy and account teams are ready. The change reassigns roles for 9,000 users and adds team members on 3 million Accounts, and the last realignment recalculated for six hours. How should the team apply it in production?

options.text: Ask Salesforce Support to enable deferred sharing, make all changes, then recalculate once
options.coachingFeedback: For objects past two million records, Customer Support can enable deferral of automatic sharing calculations, so a bulk change is applied first and recalculated once instead of once per change. A sandbox rehearsal gives the baseline for how long that run takes.

options.text: Apply the changes in nightly batches of a few regions each over several weeks
options.coachingFeedback: Each batch still starts its own recalculations, and for weeks users work under a mix of old and new models, so access differs by region and support cannot tell a defect from a pending batch.

options.text: Load the role and team changes over one weekend using parallel Bulk API jobs
options.coachingFeedback: Parallel jobs updating roles and team members contend for the same group and sharing records, which is where the lock errors came from, and every change still triggers its own recalculation.

stages.scenario: After cutover, the team must confirm each realignment's recalculation finishes within four hours, and find Accounts where branch staff lost access they need. What should the team monitor?

options.text: Recalculation durations in Background Jobs and a scheduled check for Accounts with no branch team member
options.coachingFeedback: The Background Jobs page records how long each sharing recalculation ran, which tests the four-hour window. Branch access now comes from account teams, so an Account with no branch member is exactly where access was lost.

options.text: A line-by-line review of role and sharing rule definitions against the approved design document before each realignment
options.coachingFeedback: A configuration review confirms the design is intact, but it measures neither how long recalculation runs nor whether team membership left specific Accounts uncovered.

options.text: Setup Audit Trail entries for role and sharing rule changes, reviewed by an admin after each realignment
options.coachingFeedback: Setup Audit Trail records who changed roles and sharing rules, not how long recalculation ran, and account team membership is record data that it does not track.
